title: Unable to Reproduce Radar‑Based Cooperative Detection Results & Some questions
body:
Hi authors,
Thank you for sharing the dataset and codebase.

I am trying to reproduce some radar‑based cooperative detection models using the latest code and data, but I cannot achieve the metrics reported in the README. Taking **F‑Cooper (R)** as an example:

1. When I run inference directly with the provided .pth weight file and the corresponding configuration, I obtain **AP@0.7 = 4.77 and AP@0.5 = 13.81**, which are significantly lower than the reported values (**6.84 and 23.16**, respectively).

2. I also trained the model from scratch following the official instructions, but the final performance is similar to the above and still far below the reported numbers.

In addition, I have a few questions about the dataset and code:

1. The `requirements.txt` file appears to be missing from `V2X‑Radar/CodeBase/OpenCOOD/docs/`. Could you please confirm its location or provide the required dependencies?

2. I noticed that most radar points from roadside infrastructure have **intensity = 0** and **doppler = 1**. Is this expected behaviour?

3. Some frames contain an extremely large number of radar points – for example, `train/2024‑05‑07‑19‑13‑54/142/00014_radar.pcd` has nearly **90,000** points. Is that normal for this dataset?

Any guidance would be greatly appreciated. Thank you!

title: Reproducing the LiDAR "No Fusion" baseline in Table 5 (AP@IoU=0.5 = 29.09) / AP numbers reported with BEV IoU or 3D IoU?
body: Hi authors! Thank you once again for the published dataset. ### ISSUE 1 I'm reproducing the cooperative 3D detection LiDAR baselines (Table 5) using the available configs and have a question about the No Fusion (L) row. Setup: V2X-Radar-C, opencood/tools/test.py, **collab_lidaronly_lidarpillarnet_late.yaml.** / **configs single_lidaronly_lidarpillarnet.yaml** Using your published "Late Fusion (L)" checkpoint from the Model Zoo (collab_lidaronly_lidarpillarnet_late.pth), I was able to obtain: | Case / Method | AP@0.7 / AP@0.5 (mine) | Table 5 | |--------|--------|--------| | Late Fusion| 38.8 / 66.2 | 39.37 / 65.75| The late result reproduces almost exactly, which is great but wasn't able to say the same about the No Fusion case: There are no checkpoints regarding the **"No Fusion"** method in the Modell zoo (**configs single_lidaronly_lidarpillarnet.yaml**), so I trained the model and obtained the following results that are significantly far off from the ones reported: | eval command | AP@0.7 / AP@0.5 (mine) | Table 5 | |--------|--------|--------| | No Fusion| 9.6 / 15.4 | 7.13 / 29.09 | Could you give additional insight in what is possible happening in this case? Would you have additonal info/resources that would help me achieve the reported result? Also, which checkpoint (epoch / selection criterion) corresponds to the Table 5 numbers? How is it done exactly? ### ISSUE 2 The paper and README describe "3D object detection" with "AP@IoU = 0.7 / 0.5". I'd like to confirm whether these numbers use 3D IoU or BEV (bird's-eye-view) IoU, because the released evaluation code appears to compute BEV IoU: The TP/FP matching in opencood/utils/eval_utils.py / eval_utils_modify.py (caluclate_tp_fp) uses convert_format() + compute_iou() from opencood/utils/common_utils.py: ```python # opencood/utils/common_utils.py (L257–272) def convert_format(boxes_array): """ boxes_array : (N, 4, 2) or (N, 8, 3). """ polygons = [Polygon([(box[i, 0], box[i, 1]) for i in range(4)]) for box in boxes_array] # only (x, y); z is dropped -> 2D footprint return np.array(polygons) # opencood/utils/common_utils.py (L230–254) def compute_iou(box, boxes): iou = [box.intersection(b).area / box.union(b).area for b in boxes] # 2D .area => BEV IoU return np.array(iou, dtype=np.float32) ``` Thank you for the attention! Best regards.

title: 标签的标定参数问题
body: 在您的论文中，展示出的标签重投影效果为： 而通过CodeBase中的脚本可视化出来的重投影效果为： 可以看到，CodeBase中，重投影效果和论文中展示出的存在偏差，且其它帧的重投影效果，也存在明显偏差： 且在CodeBase中，是直接将``CAM2坐标系下绕y轴的旋转``，直接转换到了``激光坐标系下绕z轴的旋转``： ``` python rot_y = -0.5 * np.pi - ry ``` 按照上述代码进行转换，其实就是默认了相机坐标系和激光坐标系之间的旋转矩阵为: ``` python R_cam2lidar=np.array([[0, 0, 1], [-1, 0, 0], [0, -1, 0]], dtype=np.float64) ``` 按照常规标注习惯，我想您们是在激光坐标系下进行的标注，即最初的目标标签是在激光坐标系下的3D Bbox，随后人为转换到了CAM2的坐标系，生成的标签文件。 所以我想明确的是，您们是如何将``激光3D Bbox``转换到``CAM2 3D Bbox``的，这种转换是否是造成上述``论文投影效果和CodeBase投影效果存在差异``的原因

title: V2X-Radar-C和V2X-Radar-I中雷达点云的差异
body:
非常感谢您杰出的工作和持续的数据更新！
我留意到V2X-Radar-C中的雷达点云是pcd格式的，它能够被正常的可视化，如[#21](https://github.com/yanglei18/V2X-Radar/issues/21)所示。V2X-Radar-I中的雷达点云是bin格式的，它似乎不能被正常的可视化，如[#5](https://github.com/yanglei18/V2X-Radar/issues/5)所示。
我读取了V2X_Radar/mini/V2X-Radar-C/train/2024-05-15-16-28-09/-1/00009_radar.pcd中的数据，发现其尺度为(7459, 3)，**3**对应每个维度的最小最大值分别为：[2.827971935272217, 389.6212158203125]，[-84.28457641601562 107.65911102294922]，[-101.54258728027344 35.653263092041016]。
同时我也读取了V2X_Radar/mini/V2X-Radar-I/training/radar/000009.bin中的数据，发现其尺度为(14918, 5)，**5**对应每个维度的最小最大值分别为：[nan, nan]，[-3.689349e+19, 3.689349e+19]，[nan, nan]，[-3.689349e+19, 3.689349e+19]，[nan, nan]。其他雷达点云bin文件也有相似的现象。
上述表明bin文件雷达点云数据存在一些问题，导致其无法被正确可视化[#5](https://github.com/yanglei18/V2X-Radar/issues/5)。请您帮忙确认一下bin格式对应的雷达点云是否正确？如果能提供V2X-Radar-I、V2X-Radar-V中pcd格式的雷达点云，那就更好了！

测试代码如下：
`
import numpy as np
import open3d as o3d

def load_radar_points_from_bin(path):
    points = np.fromfile(path, dtype=np.float32, count=-1).reshape([-1, 5])
    return points

def load_radar_points_from_pcd(path):
    pcd = o3d.io.read_point_cloud(path)
    points = np.asarray(pcd.points)
    return points

sample_idx = '00009'
radar_pcd_path = f'V2X_Radar/mini/V2X-Radar-C/train/2024-05-15-16-28-09/-1/{sample_idx}_radar.pcd'
radar_bin_path = f'V2X_Radar/mini/V2X-Radar-I/training/radar/0{sample_idx}.bin'

pcd = load_radar_points_from_pcd(radar_pcd_path)    
bin = load_radar_points_from_bin(radar_bin_path)
print(pcd.shape, pcd[:,0].min(), pcd[:,0].max(), pcd[:,1].min(), pcd[:,1].max(), pcd[:,2].min(), pcd[:,2].max())
print(bin.shape, bin[:,0].min(), bin[:,0].max(), bin[:,1].min(), bin[:,1].max(), bin[:,2].min(), bin[:,2].max(), bin[:,3].min(), bin[:,3].max(), bin[:,4].min(), bin[:,4].max())

`

title: Release V2X-Radar dataset on Hugging Face
body:
Hi @yanglei18 🤗

I'm Niels and work as part of the open-source team at Hugging Face. I discovered your work on Arxiv and was wondering whether you would like to submit it to [hf.co/papers](https://hf.co/papers) to improve its discoverability. If you are one of the authors, you can submit it at https://huggingface.co/papers/submit.

The paper page lets people discuss about your paper and lets them find artifacts about it (your dataset for instance),
you can also claim the paper as yours which will show up on your public profile at HF, add Github and project page URLs.

Would you like to host the datasets you've released on https://huggingface.co/datasets?
I see you're using a custom website for it. Hosting on Hugging Face will give you more visibility/enable better discoverability, and will also allow people to do:

```python
from datasets import load_dataset

dataset = load_dataset("your-hf-org-or-username/your-dataset")
```

If you're down, leaving a guide here: https://huggingface.co/docs/datasets/loading.
We also support Webdataset, useful for image/video datasets: https://huggingface.co/docs/datasets/en/loading#webdataset.

Besides that, there's the [dataset viewer](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/datasets-viewer) which allows people to quickly explore the first few rows of the data in the browser.

Let me know if you're interested/need any guidance.

Kind regards,

Niels
